subject: Context depth & per-1M token budget — post-call recap
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@novaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T14:12:00-04:00
Subject: Context depth & per-1M token budget — post-call recap

Hi Ayesha — thanks again for a productive conversation earlier. Quick recap and two asks so we can put a scoped PoC and pricing on paper: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Core use case: customer service agent assistant + search-assisted routing for high-value accounts.
- Peak traffic: roughly 18k sessions/day with heavy tails on a few account lookups.
- Current question: how context length choices and prompt/completion mix affect unit economics and a target budget per 1M tokens.

What I need from you to finalize pricing options: 
1) Typical average prompt tokens and completion tokens per session (ballpark is fine). If you have a small sample exported, attach — we can use anonymized rows.
2) % of sessions that require long-context documents (approx split between short <2k, medium 2k-20k, long 20k-100k+). You mentioned a few legal/contract lookups that were large; an estimate is fine.

Preliminary pricing guidance (so we’re aligned):
- If average session is ~120 prompt tokens / 420 completion tokens, cost ranges (hosted) we’d show are approximately $750–$1,100 per 1M tokens depending on model and batching.
- Long-context sessions (32k+ or 128k) increase cost primarily via memory/throughput; we model them as 3–6x the per-token execution cost for the same output due to specialized routing and lower batching efficiency.

Next steps / target timeline:
- Ayesha: send a quick sample or estimates by EOD 8/10 so we can build a 4-week PoC SKU and a firm $/1M token target.
- Marissa: I’ll follow up with a draft SOW and a couple pricing bands (PoC and committed) for TBD 8/11.
- Karthik: we may need a quick note on memory/latency tradeoffs for 32k vs 128k to include in the technical appendix.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(jordan.blake@redwood.com)

Attachment: nova_prompt-completion_profile.xlsx (template)
From: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@novaretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novaretail.com
Date: 2028-08-10T09:08:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Context depth & per-1M token budget — post-call recap

Jordan — thanks for the recap and clear asks. See quick estimates below (we can attach a sanitized export if helpful):

- Average prompt tokens per session: 95 tokens (text + a short metadata header).
- Average completion tokens per session: 370 tokens (most agent replies are concise, but some guided responses are longer).
- Session breakdown (approx): short (<2k): 82%, medium (2k–20k): 15%, long (20k–100k): 3%.
- Long sessions are mostly contract/legal lookups and multi-document synthesizes for enterprise accounts. They’re rare but business-critical.
- Monthly volume: rough active sessions 18k/day => ~540k/month. Estimated token mix (tokens/month): prompts ~51M, completions ~198M => ~249M tokens/month.

Budget guidance from procurement: baseline target is $800 per 1M tokens for hosted API during PoC. If committed we can consider a tiered arrangement.

We’ll attach a stripped export by EOD; the procurement contact is looping for budget numbers.

—Ayesha
Ayesha Khan
Head of Customer Experience | Nova Retail
ayesha.khan@novaretail.com

Attachment: nova_anonymized_sample.csv (will follow)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@novaretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@novaretail.com
Date: 2028-08-10T15:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Context depth & per-1M token budget — post-call recap

Appreciate the numbers, Ayesha — that helps a lot. I ran a quick model with your estimates and a couple of conservative assumptions: batching efficiency similar to other retail deployments, and ~4x execution overhead for long-context requests (we treat 32k patterns as 3x, 128k as 5–6x depending on cache hits). High-level outputs below (rounded):

Model A (balanced, higher perf): $/1M token = $980 (hosted)
Model B (cost-optimized: quantized medium model): $/1M token = $640 (hosted)
Committed discounted band (annual, reserved capacity): $/1M token = $420–$520 depending on commit volume and SLA tier.

With your monthly estimate (~249M tokens/month):
- PoC month at target $800/1M => ~ $199k for that month.
- If you move to committed reserved capacity at $460/1M => ~$114k/month (rough).

Key clarifications that will materially affect the numbers:
- Actual long-context mix: is 3% an accurate sustained figure or does it spike seasonally? If it spikes to 8–10% in peak periods, the per-month cost goes up ~20–40% (depending on whether we can batch or cache document prefixes).
- Average completion length distribution: are the 370 tokens mostly single-shot completions or staged multi-turns that re-send prefixes?

Proposed next steps (I’ll put these into a short thread we can use for the SOW):
1) You send the anonymized sample (Ayesha) — we’ll validate distributions and produce a per-1M token table for Model A/B and 32k/128k variants. (Target: 8/11 COB)
2) Redwood to share a draft SOW + PoC SKU and two pricing bands: hosted PoC and committed Dedicated estimate (Marissa). (Target: 8/11 morning)
3) Tech appendix with Karthik’s notes on latency/memory for 32k vs 128k and expected throughput per GPU for the PoC workload.

If these dates work I’ll attach a short cost model spreadsheet.

Thanks — Jordan

Attachment: redwood_pricing_v1.pdf (summary)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@novaretail.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@novaretail.com
Date: 2028-08-11T09:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Context depth & per-1M token budget — post-call recap

Thanks team — quick commercial note from our side:

- Jordan’s bands look reasonable vs our benchmarks. For PoC we can align to the $800/1M target if Nova provides a short commitment and the anonymized sample by EOD 8/11. That allows us to size reserved capacity for a 4-week PoC and keep the SLA simple.
- Committed pricing requires a three-month minimum reservation to deliver the $420–$520/1M band (we’ll show step-downs by volume).

Marissa (next steps):
- I’ll send a one-page PoC SOW + pricing bands and a short checklist for the anonymized export and required NDAs. Expect the DocuSign link in the next email.

If procurement wants a tighter $/1M target for the PoC (below $750) we’ll need to compress scope (lower concurrency or shorter retention on KV cache) — happy to model that if needed.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: SOW-draft-novaretail.docx (draft)
summary: Post-call sales thread: Jordan recap, customer sample estimates (avg prompt=95 / completion=370), 3% long-context sessions, procurement target $800/1M tokens for PoC. Redwood provided modeled bands (hosted $640–$980/1M; committed $420–$520/1M). Next steps: sanitized sample by 8/11, SOW + pricing, tech appendix on 32k vs 128k tradeoffs.
